Guidance & outlook: Revenue during this period almost went up by 2.75x to INR1,875 crores in FY26.
On a stand-alone basis, we maintained revenue guidance of INR1,900 crores to INR2,000 crores with the domestic business expected to grow over 20% and international business growing by over 15%.
We expect to spend between INR200 crores to INR225 crores in the capex for FY27.
Growth & demand: Stand-alone revenue for Q1 was INR431 crores, up 12.3% with domestic at INR146 crores, giving a growth of 16.2% and international at INR281.8 crores, giving a growth of 10%.

And this year, as we have added some customers, on-boarded new customers, we were able to come back to our original growth or planned growth of 17% to 18% as we had forecasted in the beginning of the year.
The reason for low growth was 32% de-growth in the Middle East due to ongoing West Asia crisis.
Margins & costs: I expect that our gross margin should continue to reflect on historic margin trend of 68% to 69% in the near term.
We have guided a stand-alone EBITDA margin of 25% to 27% for FY27, but we have delivered 28%, 100 bps higher than the guided range.
This was despite employee cost rising almost by 29%, driven by 35% increase in minimum wages in Haryana with effect from 1st April 2026, increase in headcount impacting increment for FY27.
Capex & expansion: As you all know, PolyMed initiated operations in 1997 with an IPO of INR2.65 crores using which we set up our first plant.
We did our first institutional fundraise, which resulted in multifold expansion of capacity.
Cardiology grew from INR2.9 crores to INR28.6 crores led by PendraCare acquisition together with genuine scale up of domestic business.
Balance sheet & cash: I mean PolyMed stand-alone does not have any debt other than the working capital debt.
Just I wanted to understand how much is the operating leverage, which can still play out on a longer-term basis, not just 1, 2 quarter or 1 or 2 years.
But on the working capital cycle, I think the cash conversion is still in the same level.
Risks & challenges: The rena l business was impacted by continued pricing Poly Medicu re Limited August 10, 2026 pressure from Chinese players in India, but we made a conscious choice to raise prices to push the raw material price increase rather than defend volume at any cost.
I think challenges is probably the geopolitical risk, which I see.

So hopefully, year-end, we should end with a growth of around 15% to 18% in the business, maybe close to 20%, depending on how it goes, but we are pretty confident of this growth even in spite of all the challenges we face today.

Guidance & outlook: In other words, our new higher technology segments are now contributing to over 50% of our revenue and I expect this proportion to keep on improving in coming years.
So this is our guidance for the full year of FY '27, stand-alone INR1,900 crores to INR1,950 crores and on consol basis between INR2,300 crores to INR2,400 crores.
Stand-alone EBITDA margin is expected to be -- again, we are giving a guidance of 25% to 27% range.
Growth & demand: On a full year basis, the stand-alone revenue was around INR1,662 crores, which was up by around 4% compared to previous year.
Now on the consolidated picture, full year consolidated revenue grew by 12.3% to INR1,875 crores, domestic business was around 20%, international was about 9% year-on-year.
The growth in the quarter was broadly based on domestic growth of around 25%, international business around 19%.
Margins & costs: And on the profitability, we had guided stand-alone EBITDA margin in the range of 25% to 27%.

And Q4 consolidated EBITDA were INR112 crores, a little lower than the stand-alone numbers because there was an impact of consolidation of low-margin acquisitions and about INR9 crores onetime regulatory and cost provisions in one of our international subsidiaries.

On a consolidated basis, EBITDA margin -- because our subsidiaries operate at lower EBITDA margin right now and we are in the phase of doing a lot of cost-saving projects there, so we expect this year consolidated EBITDA to be between 23% and 25%, but stand-alone will be between 25% and 27%.
Capex & expansion: Infusion Therapy now accounts for 50% of the revenue, down from 57% in Q4 '25 with Renal around 11%, steadily rising, share coming from Cardiology, Critical Care and other acquisitions.
For FY '26, the capex was around INR296 crores pertaining to our plants Haridwar, Faridabad, Mitrol and also in YEIDA Medical Park.
We expect to spend between INR200 crores to INR225 crores on capex this year.
Balance sheet & cash: This amount is a strategic reserve for our strategic initiatives in future, and we intend to use operating cash flows to meet regular capex requirements across the group.
But if we see from the perspective of the days, inventory days has increased from 50 to 58 days.
And apart from inventory days, if you see the receivables, which has increased drastically from, let's say, INR340 crores to INR440 crores.
Risks & challenges: We have seen the current disruption caused by Gulf war, and I think the situation is quite challenging.
And we see there was an impact of around 20% on an aggregate basis in raw materials and a meaningful headwind to the gross margin.

In spite of all the headwinds and challenging situation, we are still guiding higher so that -- because today, the demand is coming back, what we had lost earlier in the last year, and also Indian market, I think we can see our presence now in all -- most of the corporate chains, larger hospitals and even in standalone hospitals.

guidance.t: And on the profitability, we had guided stand-alone EBITDA margin in the range of 25% to 27%.
On stand-alone basis, we are guiding on a revenue of INR1,900 crores to INR1950 crores with domestic business growing upwards of 20% and international business growing upwards of 15%.
We expect to spend between INR200 crores to INR225 crores on capex this year.
